source.title: Confirming Claims of Superposition and Adversarial Examples in Toy Models

page_placements.theme: Superposition geometry, adversarial vulnerability and robustness

record.file_problem: The prose and tables are present, but several inline equations and mathematical symbols are missing from the web text.
record.tranche_reason: It reports results from toy bottleneck classifiers about feature geometry under superposition-related conditions, using experiments that differ from the original Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.gate_note: The PGD alignment, random-direction comparisons, robust-accuracy sweep, cross-seed geometry and transfer results, and paired-feature geometry sweep are reported results. The referenced paper's values are not extracted as this study's results. The article also describes methods and figures whose numerical values are not present in the text; those are recorded as figure only where the text states the outcome.
record.test_reason: The study mainly replicates Stevinson et al. on adversarial attacks, which has no matching version. Its added experiment sweeps co-activation coupling across bottleneck widths in toy classifiers. It reports whether superposed features stay near-orthogonal or collapse, which bears on V1's geometry, using a different model (cross-entropy classifier) from the original.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but incomplete. The authors say they reproduce all three Stevinson et al. claims: PGD matches optimal interference attacks, robustness falls as superposition rises, and attacks transfer because geometries converge under correlation. They add that co-activating features collapse onto shared directions when capacity is lacking and stay near-orthogonal when it is slack. They frame this collapse as similar to what Elhage et al. reported, not as contradicting it.
record.recipe_differences: The article replicates Stevinson et al.'s adversarial-attack experiments, not the original Toy Models of Superposition study. It uses an encoder-decoder toy classifier with a bottleneck, cross-entropy loss, and PGD attacks, and adds paired-feature geometry sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported feature geometry changes with input-correlation regime, paired-feature coupling, and bottleneck capacity.

fits_no_version.finding: PGD perturbations align with the closed-form optimal interference-exploiting perturbation (cosine 1.00). Random directions give near-zero similarity, and successful random directions give lower similarity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial attacks on toy superposition models exploit feature interference geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Robust accuracy falls monotonically as k/m rises: from 100% to 18.7% at m=2, and from 97.3% to 30.1% at m=5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Toy models with more superposition are less adversarially robust.

fits_no_version.finding: Between-seed geometric similarity and targeted attack transfer grow with input correlation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input correlation drives geometry convergence across runs, and with it attack transfer.

fits_no_version.finding: Targeted attack success rises with head interference pair by pair.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pairwise interference predicts pairwise adversarial vulnerability in toy models.

record.problems: Several mathematical expressions and symbols are missing in the web text. Numerical values for geometry and transfer plots are only available as figures, and the text notes magnitude gaps from the referenced paper due to different training steps and attack parameters.
record.rows_left_out: The table's Paper reported and Released code comparison columns were not recorded as this study's own outcomes. Other figure-only details without a distinct stated result were omitted.

untested.parts: No sparsity sweep, so no sparsity-dependent phase transition. No regular polytope geometry for independent sparse features. Superposition pressure is varied only through k/m and coupling.
Entire version: no neuron-level polysemanticity or importance-based allocation.
Entire version: no LLMs and no SAEs.

missing.what: At an intermediate bottleneck width, partner cosine crosses above the non-partner baseline at a particular coupling t. This gives a capacity-dependent threshold for collapse, but the t value is lost in the web text.
missing.locator: Beyond Replication: Orthogonalize or Collapse?, Figure 5 caption

missing.what: In the uncorrelated regime, class-vector arrangements are random relative to each other across seeds. This is the baseline for R3 and R4.

record.verdict_notes: I replaced the reader's 'challenges' label on V1 with 'limits_scope': the collapse concerns correlated features, and the authors explicitly say the original reports the same thing. All V1 geometry evidence is figure-only and qualitative, and the capacity thresholds are lost because equations are missing from the web text. The source is a LessWrong post replication, not peer reviewed.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not sweep feature sparsity or establish a sparsity-dependent transition. Its feature-geometry experiment varies paired-feature coupling and bottleneck capacity instead.
It does not study neuron polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
It does not investigate polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
It does not study LLM feature distributions or sparse features recovered by a dictionary.
It does not assess whether dictionary features are complete, stable, or canonical.
It does not compare one-dimensional and multidimensional features. The reported class-vector geometry does not test the dimensionality of the represented features.

statements.problem: For this study the tilt/collapse claim is stated for the low width (m=2, k=7) only; the plot shows partial alignment (partner cos about 0.5) below the non-partner |cos| baseline of about 0.6, so literal collapse is stated in prose, not shown by the figure. m=3,4 (also k/m>1) are put by the text in the near-orthogonal/avoidance regime. Cyclic-covariance, bag-of-words, WikiText and transformer parts are not from this study.
